summary: Dan Lusthaus, a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earned his Ph.D. from Temple University under several teachers including Charles Wei-hsun Fu. He taught at multiple institutions, including Florida State University (attested 1997) and the University of Georgia (attested 2000).

Dan Martin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington (~1984–1991) under Elliot Sperling, and held positions at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters (~1995–1996) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1996–1998).

Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Davis and served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who completed his Ph.D. at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet (~1991–1994) and his Habilitation at the University of Copenhagen. He led the Center for Subjectivity Research (~2002–2017) and was a professor at Oxford (2018–2021).

Daniel Aaron Getz, active in Buddhist studies and sinology, earned his Ph.D. from Yale University (attested 1994) under Stanley Weinstein, Ying-shih Yü, and Tairyo Makita. He held an associate professorship at Bradley University (attested 2019).
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Daniel B. Stevenson, a specialist in Buddhist studies and sinology, earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University. He held assistant professor posts at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003).
Daniel Baum is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and completed his doctorate at Leiden University (~2000–2006) under Alexander Lubotsky and Saul Migron.
Daniel Borengasser, a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology, earned his Master of Arts at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington and earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (-1996) under Victor H. Mair, later serving as associate professor at Cornell University (attested 2000–2008, 2026).

Daniel Clarke Waugh works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Yale University (B.A. 1963) and Harvard University (master's 1965, degree 1972) before joining the University of Washington faculty in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale (1856–1872), president of the University of California (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution (1902–1904).

Daniel Cozort works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (~1980–1989) under Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teachers, later becoming an assistant professor of religion at Dickinson College (~1989).

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a director of research at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (~1983–2015) and held a post at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III.

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Harvard University under Walter Eugene Clark and W. V. Quine, as well as with Kalipada Tarkacharya. He served as a professor at Harvard University from 1939.

Daniel John Gogerly was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He oversaw the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818–1822), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society in 1838, and served as secretary, vice-president, and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1845–1858).

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973–2001).

Daniel M. Neuman, an Indologist and ethnomusicologist, studied at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago. He taught at Dartmouth College (1971–1980), University of Washington (1980–1995), and University of California, Los Angeles (~1994–2018).

Daniel M. Stuart specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2012) under Alexander von Rospatt and held posts at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017) and University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Daniel P. Brown was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Geshe Wangyal and served as a professor at Harvard University from approximately 1975 to 2021.
